mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which compresses profit margins and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met in a walk-forward validation.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies decline for two quarters in out-of-sample data.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases uncertainty and risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both above 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both inflation and rates exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% signals a robust labor market recovery, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS jumps by more than 0.5% in a month during recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals that households are drawing down savings to maintain consumption, which increases debt risk and reduces equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently below its 12-month average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall for two consecutive months in out-of-sample periods.
